summary: An application blueprint for polylogarithmic zeta determinants, with an explicit finite-dimensional determinant argument, rational and integral convention boundaries, a source-audited low-weight proof plan, and declaration-sized initial configuration and cycle-lifting lemmas. The weight-three and weight-four proof-specific maps and their regulator comparisons are not fully decomposed here. Their missing subtrees are recorded as gaps rather than concealed inside an assumed motivic isomorphism. The packet is not ready for mathematical closure or integration as a completed blueprint.

nodes.title: Parity-dependent size and period exponent
nodes.statement: For a number field F of signature (r1,r2) and integer n>=2, define d(F,n)=r2 and e(F,n)=n(r1+r2) when n is even, and d(F,n)=r1+r2 and e(F,n)=n*r2 when n is odd. For a positive real D define P(F,n,D)=pi^e(F,n)/sqrt(D). The special-value application supplies D=abs(discriminant(F)); D is not an unconstrained normalization parameter there.
hypotheses: F is a number field
D>0 for the period factor
proofSteps: Use the two pinned cardinality abbreviations for r1 and r2, and make the two parity branches explicit.
Use the ordinary real power and positive square root for P. Its nonvanishing follows from D>0 and pi>0 by real arithmetic.
acceptance: At (r1,r2)=(1,0), weights two and four have d=0 and e=2,4.
At an imaginary quadratic signature (0,1), d=1 for every n and e=n.

nodes.title: Nonzero rational proportionality
nodes.statement: For x,y in R define RationalProportional x y to mean there is q in Q, q!=0, with x=q*y. Zero is proportional only to zero. A determinant which may vanish is instead handled by an explicitly possibly-zero rational coefficient.
proofSteps: Use the injective embedding Q into R in the existential equality.
Reflexivity uses q=1, symmetry uses q inverse, and transitivity uses multiplication of witnesses.
acceptance: RationalProportional 0 1 is false.
No nonzero requirement is dropped when converting a full-rank determinant identity.

api.name: Zagier.RationalProportional

api.name: Zagier.RationalProportional.symm

api.name: Zagier.RationalProportional.trans

nodes.title: Columns of an evaluated tuple
nodes.statement: For a Q-vector space W, finite index type I, Q-linear lambda:W->(I->R), and tuple x:I->W, define M(lambda,x) by M(i,j)=lambda(x_j)(i). The first index is the embedding row and the second is the cycle column.
hypotheses: I is finite and has decidable equality
lambda is Q-linear
proofSteps: Define the matrix entrywise, using the existing matrix carrier rather than a new matrix wrapper.
Coordinate extensionality gives equality of matrices from equality of their entries; linearity gives the column formulas.
acceptance: A tuple indexed by an empty I produces the unique empty square matrix.
No ordering of all complex embeddings is silently imposed.

nodes.title: A comparison scalar acts in every column
nodes.statement: For a square real matrix M indexed by a finite type I of cardinality d and a real scalar a, det(a*M)=a^d*det(M), where a*M means entrywise scalar multiplication. The formula includes d=0.
hypotheses: I is finite and has decidable equality
proofSteps: Expand det using Matrix.det_apply.
Every permutation summand has exactly d entries, so its product gains a^d. Factor this out of the finite sum.
For d=0 the factor is a^0=1, including a=0; do not use a theorem saying the zero matrix has determinant zero without a nonempty index.
acceptance: For d=2 the comparison factor is a squared, not a.
The empty determinant remains one.

sources.match: Direct finite-product argument from the checked formula.

nodes.title: Rational changes of columns
nodes.statement: Let x and y be I-tuples in W and A a rational I-by-I matrix with y_j=sum_k A(k,j)*x_k. Then M(lambda,y)=M(lambda,x)*A_R and det M(lambda,y)=det M(lambda,x)*(det A)_R. Invertibility of A is required only when the rational factor must be nonzero.
hypotheses: lambda is Q-linear
I is finite and has decidable equality
The displayed column relation holds
proofSteps: Evaluate each column relation with lambda and compare entries with matrix multiplication.
Apply Matrix.det_mul.
Expand the rational determinant by Matrix.det_apply; preservation of finite sums, products and integer signs under Q->R gives det(A_R)=(det A)_R.
acceptance: A singular rational A is allowed and produces zero determinant.
The column formula uses A(k,j), not its transpose.

sources.match: Exact determinant identities at the pin; the rational-cast calculation is the stated finite algebraic reduction.

nodes.title: Signed changes of embedding rows
nodes.statement: If M' is obtained from a real square matrix M by a permutation sigma of rows and multiplication of each row i by epsilon_i in {1,-1}, then det(M')=sign(sigma)*(product_i epsilon_i)*det(M). Thus this change preserves nonzero rational proportionality, including the empty case.
hypotheses: The row operation is exactly the specified signed permutation
proofSteps: Apply Matrix.det_permute to the row permutation, checking its submatrix sigma id statement.
Represent row signs by left multiplication by the diagonal matrix epsilon and apply det_mul and det_diagonal.
The sign and every epsilon_i are rational units; their empty product is one.
acceptance: Replacing one complex embedding by its conjugate changes the sign in even weight, once the functional parity theorem has been supplied.
Row and column conventions are not interchanged.

sources.match: The actual first-index permutation statement supplies the required row convention.

nodes.title: Transfer of an existential determinant identity
nodes.statement: Let V,W be Q-vector spaces, r:V->R^I, lambda:W->R^I and c:V->W be Q-linear, and let a,q be nonzero rationals. If lambda composed with c=a*r and z=P*q*det M(r,v) for an I-tuple v, then z=P*(q/a^d)*det M(lambda,c composed with v), where d=card(I). Surjectivity of c is not needed.
hypotheses: I is finite
a,q are nonzero rationals
The two displayed equalities hold
proofSteps: The comparison equality gives M(lambda,c v)=a*M(r,v) entry by entry.
Apply determinant-scalar to get the factor a^d.
Multiply the starting equality by (a^d)/(a^d), which is legitimate because a is nonzero. The new rational coefficient is q/a^d.
acceptance: No assertion that c is an isomorphism or that W has dimension d is used.
For d=0 the new coefficient remains q.

sources.locator: Finite determinant formula; application to a scalar matrix equality
sources.match: The transfer theorem is an elementary derivation here, not a claim that a regulator comparison has already been proved.

nodes.title: Rationality for every tuple needs image control
nodes.statement: Let v be an I-tuple in V with det M(r,v)!=0, and assume lambda(W) is contained in the Q-linear span of the vectors r(v_j). For every I-tuple x in W there is b in Q with det M(lambda,x)=b*det M(r,v). If det M(lambda,x)!=0, then b!=0. Consequently z=P*q*det M(r,v), with z,P nonzero and q in Q nonzero, implies P*det M(lambda,x)/z is rational for every x.
hypotheses: The stated containment is in a Q-span, not merely an R-span
det M(r,v)!=0
z and P are nonzero for the ratio statement
proofSteps: For each of finitely many columns choose rational coefficients expressing lambda(x_j) in the specified span.
Collect them as a rational matrix A. Apply rational-column-change to the evaluated vectors in R^I.
Set b=det A. Nonzero determinants force b!=0; the final ratio is b/q.
acceptance: A forward comparison V->W alone is not accepted as the span hypothesis.
All tuples includes linearly dependent tuples; b may then be zero.

sources.locator: Matrix.det_mul, applied to a matrix of rational coordinates
sources.match: The proof isolates the additional image-containment hypothesis instead of attributing it to Borel's rank theorem.

nodes.title: Absorbing a rational factor requires a column
nodes.statement: If I is nonempty, lambda is Q-linear and z=P*q*det M(lambda,x) with q in Q, replacing a selected column x_j0 by q*x_j0 gives an exact equation z=P*det M(lambda,y). No such conclusion follows for an empty I by this operation.
hypotheses: I is finite and nonempty
A selected j0 in I is given
proofSteps: Use rational-column-change with the diagonal rational matrix having q at j0 and one elsewhere.
Its determinant is q by det_diagonal.
For empty I there is no j0, and every determinant is one by det_isEmpty.
acceptance: The uniform number-field statement retains q even though positive-rank specializations can absorb it.

sources.match: Makes the nonempty-index hypothesis of the rescaling argument explicit.

nodes.title: The rational field regression
nodes.statement: For F=Q and n=2 or 4, the regulator determinant has size zero, hence equals one. With discriminant one the rational-factor formulation specializes to zeta(2)=q*pi^2 and zeta(4)=q*pi^4; the classical values give q=1/6 and 1/90. A uniform q-free equality would fail these tests.
hypotheses: Use the stated classical evaluations, not floating-point evidence
proofSteps: Insert r1=1,r2=0 into signature-profile.
Apply det_isEmpty.
Compare with the two exact evaluations printed on Zagier p. 392.
acceptance: No empty determinant is assigned zero.
Do not change the definition of P or the determinant to force q=1.

sources.match: Both exact classical evaluations and the rational-prefactor discussion were visually read; formal-library evaluation declarations have not been claimed.

nodes.title: Bloch-Wigner evaluation on the supplied rational quotient
nodes.statement: For a number field F, extend D(sigma(a)) Q-linearly to finite formal combinations of admissible symbols a in F minus {0,1}; using the supplied five-term identity, descend to the rational pre-Bloch quotient. Restrict this map to the supplied Bloch kernel and assemble one component for each selected complex embedding. This does not construct D or redefine the quotient.
hypotheses: The supplier's precise five-term quotient and boundary convention have been fixed
D satisfies that five-term relation
Complex embeddings are explicitly selected
proofSteps: Extend on the free rational symbol module by finite summation.
Every relation generator maps to zero by the supplied functional equation, so use the quotient universal property.
Restrict to the kernel of the supplied boundary and assemble the embedding components.
acceptance: A symbol can be evaluated in the pre-Bloch group without being a Bloch cycle; use a boundary certificate before calling it a cycle.
Torsion is not detected by this real-valued map.

nodes.title: Real rows vanish and complex representatives change sign
nodes.statement: The Bloch-Wigner evaluation vanishes at every real embedding and changes sign when a complex embedding is replaced by its conjugate. Consequently the weight-two determinant indexed by complex places is independent of these choices up to a sign.
hypotheses: The supplier proves D(conjugate z)=-D(z) on its complete domain, including extended boundary values
proofSteps: Apply the supplied conjugation identity termwise to a finite symbol representative.
At a real embedding the value equals its negative and is therefore zero in R.
Use signed-row-change for different choices and orderings of complex representatives.
acceptance: No real embedding contributes a weight-two row.
The argument takes place in R, so division by two is legitimate; it says nothing about integral 2-torsion.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 394–395, properties of the Bloch-Wigner function
sources.match: The requested conjugation law is applied to the existing function; quotient and row consequences are elementary.

nodes.title: Rationalizing a map with torsion kernel and cokernel
nodes.statement: For a homomorphism f:A->B of abelian groups whose kernel and cokernel are torsion, f tensor Q is an isomorphism. This is a statement about the induced map, not an arbitrary isomorphism between vector spaces of equal dimension.
hypotheses: Every element of ker f and coker f has some positive integer annihilator
proofSteps: For surjectivity, a class of b in coker f is killed by an integer m>0, so m*b=f(a); b tensor 1 is the image of a tensor (1/m).

For injectivity, represent a rationalized element by a single denominator. If its image vanishes, a nonzero integer multiple of its numerator maps to zero. Another nonzero integer kills that element of ker f, so the original rationalized element vanishes.
The inverse is the inverse of the induced bijective Q-linear map, which is automatically natural in commuting squares.
acceptance: No uniform annihilating integer for the whole kernel is required.
The integral map need not be an isomorphism.

sources.match: Elementary rationalization lemma needed to apply the displayed torsion-kernel sequence. It is derived here, not attributed as a separately numbered theorem in Suslin.

nodes.title: The rational Suslin comparison
nodes.statement: For an infinite field F, rationalize the supplier's canonical map K3ind(F)->B_Sus(F) in the Bloch-Wigner exact sequence to obtain a natural Q-linear equivalence K3ind(F)_Q -> B_Sus(F)_Q. The enhanced Tor group in the kernel is used as stated, not replaced by ordinary Tor before rationalization.
hypotheses: F is infinite
The supplier provides Suslin's enhanced-torsion exact sequence and the torsion property of its kernel
proofSteps: Apply rationalization-torsion to the supplied surjection and its enhanced-torsion kernel.
Retain the induced map as the forward equivalence and characterize its inverse by the two inverse identities.
Naturality follows from the supplied naturality square and uniqueness of the inverse.
acceptance: No use of this infinite-field theorem at small finite fields.
The integral enhanced Tor extension remains available to consumers needing torsion.

nodes.title: Removing the decomposable part over a number field
nodes.statement: For a number field F, the canonical quotient K3(F)->K3ind(F) induces a rational equivalence, using the supplier's theorem that Milnor K3(F) is torsion. Its composition with suslinRationalEquiv is the rational K3-to-Suslin-Bloch comparison.
hypotheses: F is a number field
K3ind is the cokernel of Milnor K3->Quillen K3
The torsion theorem for Milnor K3(F) is supplied
proofSteps: The kernel of the quotient is the image of Milnor K3, hence is torsion; the quotient is surjective by construction.
Apply rationalization-torsion and compose with suslinRationalEquiv.
Use only the image of Milnor K3; injectivity of the product map is not assumed.
acceptance: Do not identify Milnor K3 with a subgroup unless injection has separately been proved.
The number-field torsion input is not silently generalized to arbitrary infinite fields.

nodes.title: Transport from Suslin's kernel to the chosen weight-two cycles
nodes.statement: Use the supplier's rational comparison square between Suslin's pre-Bloch presentation and the chosen B2(F), together with the rational antisymmetric-tensor-to-exterior-square equivalence, to identify B_Sus(F)_Q with Z2(F)=ker(delta2). Fix delta2{x}=(1-x) wedge x and include the sign relating this to Suslin's boundary. The comparison preserves the symbol evaluation D after the specified source-model transport.
hypotheses: The comparison square is commutative with its sign fixed
Both vertical maps in the rational boundary square are equivalences
Evaluation is compatible on generators
proofSteps: Restrict the two vertical equivalences in the boundary square to their kernels.
Kernel membership is preserved and reflected by commutativity and injectivity of the boundary-target equivalence.
Transport D by its generator formula, not by an inference that equality of real regulators detects integral classes.
acceptance: The antisymmetric tensor quotient is not declared to be the exterior square integrally.
Different higher relation models are not identified merely because their real evaluations agree.

nodes.title: The exact Borel determinant input
nodes.statement: For a number field F and n>=2, put V=K_(2n-1)(F)_Q and d=d(F,n). Under the requested, period-normalized Borel interface, there is a rational basis v indexed by d with det M(r_n,v)!=0 and a nonzero rational q such that zeta_F(n)=P(F,n,abs(disc F))*q*det M(r_n,v). The image of r_n is the rational span of those columns. The normalized r_n must come from the supplier's constructed regulator, not be defined using a desired polylogarithm comparison.
hypotheses: The Borel rank, regulator lattice and special-value theorems are all supplied
The comparison between arithmetic and field K-groups and the real/Tate coordinate convention have been proved
The positive-integer value agrees with NumberField.dedekindZeta on its convergent domain
proofSteps: Use the rational field/arithmetic K-theory comparison and the regulator lattice to choose an arithmetic basis modulo torsion and hence a rational basis of V.
Apply the supplier's zeta theorem, its functional-equation normalization and orientation convention to that basis.
The columns are real-linearly independent because the regulator is a full lattice after real scalar extension. Every rational K-class has rational basis coordinates, giving the last image statement.
acceptance: Rank alone cannot replace the lattice and zeta statements.
The original Borel normalization and the adopted real coordinate must be compared explicitly; see G-NORMALIZATION.
Do not evaluate a totalized L-series at 1-n and call it analytic continuation.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.2, Remark 6.3 and section 6.4, printed pp. 631–633
sources.match: The lattice/zeta theorem is distinct from the rank calculation. The exact translation to P is an unclosed normalization request, not asserted as checked.
The desired real-coordinate rational proportionality is formulated here.

nodes.statement: For the composite c2:K3(F)_Q->Z2(F) of the number-field quotient, rational Suslin map and rational cycle-model comparison, prove lambda2 composed with c2=a2*r2 with a2 a nonzero rational in the fixed real coordinate. This is a target with an unresolved proof subtree G-DILOG, not a consequence of equality of ranks.
hypotheses: All model and period conventions in the prerequisite maps are fixed
proofSteps: Construct the cross-ratio/configuration cocycle representing D on the homological K3 model and compare its map with the supplied Suslin map.
Identify its continuous-cohomology class with the normalized Borel class through the hyperbolic-volume or Chern-class calculation.

Transcribe the scalar and orientation and prove it is the required nonzero rational after the chosen real/Tate conversion. The proof-specific configuration and normalization lemmas remain to be split and checked in G-DILOG.
acceptance: Neither a nonzero real scalar nor equality of abstract one-dimensional cohomology spaces is sufficient.
No integral Bloch isomorphism is inferred from this real comparison.

sources.match: The relevant theorem and model distinctions were read, but not a complete map-level proof with its scalar. This node remains blocked by G-DILOG.

nodes.title: Weight-two determinant existence
nodes.statement: Once the listed comparison nodes are proved, every number field F has d(F,2) rational Bloch cycles x_j and q in Q nonzero with zeta_F(2)=P(F,2,abs(disc F))*q*det(D(sigma_i(x_j))). This remains a blocked target while G-DILOG and the supplier requests are open.
hypotheses: F is a number field
Use the fixed complex-place coordinates
proofSteps: Choose v and the rational coefficient from borel-matrix-input at n=2.
Set x_j=c2(v_j) using the specified maps.
Apply existential-transfer with the scalar a2 from dilogarithmic-regulator-comparison. The new coefficient is q/a2^d.
acceptance: Real fields with d=0 are included.
Each x_j carries an actual vanishing-boundary condition.

sources.match: The determinant consequence is assembled explicitly, without treating the still-open comparison proof as completed.

nodes.title: Rationality for all weight-two cycle tuples
nodes.statement: Under the same completed comparisons, for every d(F,2)-tuple x of rational Bloch cycles the real number P(F,2,abs(disc F))*det M(lambda2,x)/zeta_F(2) lies in Q. It is nonzero exactly when the determinant is nonzero.
hypotheses: The rational K3-to-cycle comparison is surjective, indeed an equivalence
The Borel input and regulator comparison have been proved
proofSteps: Lift each x_j through the rational equivalence c2.
Express the lifts in the rational basis v from borel-matrix-input, then multiply their regulator columns by the rational scalar a2.
Apply all-tuples-transfer. Surjectivity here is furnished by the actual weight-two equivalence, unlike a mere forward map in higher weight.
acceptance: Dependent tuples give rational value zero and are not excluded.
The argument does not generalize to n=3 or 4 until the extra image-control input is supplied.

sources.match: Rational surjectivity is supplied by this map, not by regulator equality alone.

nodes.title: The first-cycle carrier
nodes.statement: For a supplied rational polylogarithmic complex Gamma(F,n) with B_n(F) in cohomological degree one, define Z_n(F) as the kernel of its first differential. Use delta2{x}=(1-x) wedge x and delta_n{x}={x}_(n-1) tensor x for n>2 on admissible symbols, with the supplier's explicit special-value conventions at 0,1,infinity. Z_n is a subspace of B_n, not B_n itself.
hypotheses: The particular relation model, complex, and special-value conventions are supplied
proofSteps: Take the kernel of the existing first linear differential; do not construct a second symbol quotient.
Use the canonical inclusion and the kernel condition as the constructor/eliminator interface.
Commuting field-embedding squares restrict to maps on these kernels.
acceptance: A formal sum with no boundary certificate is not automatically a cycle.
The symbol at 1 is not uniformly killed in odd weights.

api.name: Zagier.firstCycles
api.statement: The kernel subspace of the supplier's first differential.

api.name: Zagier.firstCycles.mk
api.statement: Build a cycle from b in B_n with delta_n(b)=0.

api.name: Zagier.firstCycles.ext
api.statement: Cycles with equal underlying B_n elements are equal.

api.name: Zagier.firstCycles.map
api.statement: A field embedding induces the restricted kernel map, with identity and composition laws.

api.name: Zagier.firstCycles.mem_iff
api.statement: Membership is precisely vanishing of the supplied first differential.

sources.locator: Section 1.4, relation quotients; section 3 diagram (3.2), pp. 16–17
sources.match: Fixes the complex and first-cycle distinction; a weight-four extension of the reserved supplier contract is explicitly requested.

nodes.title: First cohomology has no incoming boundaries
nodes.statement: For the supplied Gamma(F,n), whose term in degree zero is zero, the canonical map Z_n(F)->H^1(Gamma(F,n)) is a Q-linear equivalence, natural in field embeddings. This is an elementary complex calculation, not a motivic K-theory comparison.
hypotheses: The degree-zero term is zero
proofSteps: The image of the incoming differential 0->B_n is zero.
First cohomology is therefore the quotient of the first kernel by its zero subspace.
Identify this quotient with the kernel and verify naturality using the inclusion maps.
acceptance: No quotient by unmentioned incoming relations remains in H^1.
The equivalence does not identify this group with K_(2n-1).

sources.match: The displayed degree convention makes the kernel/cohomology identification immediate; it is not the conjectural motivic comparison.

nodes.title: Embedding-wise evaluation of higher cycles
nodes.statement: For the supplier's real-valued single-valued L_n, extend L_n(sigma(a)) Q-linearly to the rational symbol module, descend using the proved relation-annihilation theorem for the selected B_n model, then restrict to Z_n(F). The resulting lambda_n:Z_n(F)->R^I uses complex-place representatives and, in odd weight, real embeddings as rows.
hypotheses: L_n annihilates the actual relation space defining B_n
The real coordinate uses odd real part and even imaginary part, with Bernoulli convention B1=-1/2
proofSteps: For each embedding extend by finite summation and apply the quotient universal property.
Restrict the descended functional to the first kernel.
Assemble the finite row family and use the supplier's conjugation parity to compare row choices.
acceptance: Use the relation model's proven functional-equation theorem, not experimental numerical agreement.
No division by a Tate period is inserted without an explicit coordinate comparison.

api.name: Zagier.cycleEvaluation
api.statement: The Q-linear lambda_n in the selected row coordinates.

api.name: Zagier.cycleEvaluation_symbols
api.statement: For a certified finite symbol combination, evaluation is its finite weighted sum of L_n values.

api.name: Zagier.cycleEvaluation_embedding
api.statement: Evaluate after a field embedding by composing that embedding with each complex embedding.

api.name: Zagier.cycleEvaluation_conjugate
api.statement: A conjugated row gains (-1)^(n-1); odd-weight real rows remain and even-weight real rows vanish.

sources.match: The inspected proof proves relation descent by a differential identity and specialization; the supplier must provide it for the same model.

nodes.title: A constructor from a finite boundary certificate
nodes.statement: Given a finite rational symbol combination s and a proof delta_n([s])=0 in the supplier's boundary target, define cycleOfSymbols(s) in Z_n(F) with underlying class [s]. Two certified combinations produce the same cycle exactly when their classes agree in the supplied B_n quotient. No alternative equivalence relation or new cycle carrier is introduced.
hypotheses: A finite representative and its vanishing-boundary proof are supplied
proofSteps: Map s through the supplier's quotient map and pair its class with the boundary proof.
Use equality in the kernel subtype to reduce equality of cycles to equality in B_n.
Addition and rational scaling use the linearity of the quotient and differential.
acceptance: Clearing rational coefficients alone is not called an integral Bloch-cycle proof: residual torsion in an integral boundary may require another multiplier.
Certificates transport along field embeddings through the supplied differential square.

api.name: Zagier.cycleOfSymbols
api.statement: Construct a cycle from a finite combination and a boundary certificate.

api.name: Zagier.cycleOfSymbols_val
api.statement: Its underlying B_n class is the quotient of the given combination.

api.name: Zagier.cycleOfSymbols_eq_iff
api.statement: Equality is precisely equality of the underlying quotient classes.

api.name: Zagier.cycleOfSymbols_add
api.statement: The constructor respects addition and rational scalar multiplication of certified combinations.

sources.locator: Introduction, definition of B_n and kernel in Theorem 1.2, pp. 4–5
sources.match: The actual cycle condition is on the quotient's first differential, not a list of numerical evaluations.

nodes.title: The generic ordered configuration carrier
nodes.statement: Let F be a field and V an n-dimensional F-vector space with n>0. Gen(V,m) is the type of ordered m-tuples of vectors such that each subtuple of length at most n is linearly independent. GL(V) acts diagonally. Use C_k=Q[Gen(V,k+1)] for k>=0; this is the source's configuration module on k+1 vectors, not its coinvariant module.
hypotheses: V has finite dimension n>0
proofSteps: Define the genericity predicate on actual finite tuples by linear independence of each admissible subtuple.
An invertible linear map preserves and reflects linear independence, giving the diagonal action.
Form the free rational vector space on this carrier; the index shift is recorded before constructing its differential.
acceptance: A tuple longer than n may be generic; only its subtuples of length at most n are tested.
Coinvariants are a separate construction and are not automatically an exact resolution.

api.name: Zagier.GenericConfiguration
api.statement: An ordered tuple with the specified subtuple independence property.

api.name: Zagier.GenericConfiguration.ext
api.statement: Equality is entrywise equality of vectors.

api.name: Zagier.GenericConfiguration.map
api.statement: Transport along a linear equivalence, with identity and composition laws.

api.name: Zagier.GenericConfiguration.erase
api.statement: Delete one entry, retaining genericity by the subtuple condition.

api.name: Zagier.configurationModule
api.statement: The free rational module on generic (k+1)-tuples with the induced GL(V)-action.

sources.match: The carrier and degree shift follow the displayed construction. Baseline free-module and group-action declarations still need the additional source audit in G-BASELINE.

nodes.title: Alternating deletion with augmentation
nodes.statement: Define the Q-linear boundary of a generic tuple by the sum of its deletions with coefficient (-1)^i, indexing entries from zero. For degree zero use the augmentation sending every one-vector generator to 1 in Q. Regard Q as degree -1 only for this augmented-chain calculation.
hypotheses: The generic-configuration carrier has been constructed
proofSteps: Deletion preserves genericity; extend the alternating finite sum linearly from generators.
Define the augmentation by the constant value one on generators.
Check that linear equivalences commute with every deletion, hence the boundary and augmentation are GL(V)-equivariant.
acceptance: The augmentation kernel, not all C_0, is the cycle space in augmented degree zero.
The source's m-vector generator has homological degree m-1.

api.name: Zagier.configurationBoundary
api.statement: The linear alternating-deletion map.

api.name: Zagier.configurationBoundary_generator
api.statement: Its value on a generator is the stated signed deletion sum.

api.name: Zagier.configurationAugmentation
api.statement: Send each degree-zero generator to 1.

api.name: Zagier.configurationBoundary_equivariant
api.statement: The boundary commutes with the diagonal GL(V)-action.

sources.match: Uses the displayed differential with an explicit zero-based indexing translation.

nodes.title: Two deletions cancel
nodes.statement: Successive configuration boundaries compose to zero, and the augmentation composed with the degree-one boundary is zero.
proofSteps: On each generator pair the term deleting positions i then j with the term deleting the same two original positions in the opposite order.
The reindexing changes the sign by one, while the resulting ordered tuple is identical.
For a two-vector tuple, the augmentation of its boundary is 1-1=0; extend linearly.
acceptance: Test the three-vector boundary with all six signed two-step deletions.
The proof does not use a quotient by GL(V).

sources.match: Elementary verification of the differential used in Lemma 3.1.

nodes.title: Avoid finitely many proper linear subspaces
nodes.statement: Over an infinite field F, a finite union of proper linear subspaces of a vector space V is not all of V.
hypotheses: F is infinite
Each subspace in the finite family is proper
proofSteps: Induct on the size of the family. Choose v outside the earlier subspaces by induction and w outside the last subspace by properness.

On the line v+t*w, each earlier subspace excludes all but at most one parameter: if two parameters land in it, subtraction puts w and then v in it, a contradiction. The same at-most-one conclusion holds for the last subspace because w is outside it.
Choose t outside the finite set of exceptional parameters, using infinitude of F.
acceptance: The statement is not used over a finite field.
No compactness or topology is involved.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.1, p. 16, choice of a vector in general position
sources.match: The source's generic-vector choice is expanded into this elementary finite-avoidance lemma.

nodes.title: The augmented configuration complex is acyclic
nodes.statement: For infinite F and n>0, every cycle in the augmented rational configuration complex is a boundary. Thus the unaugmented complex has H_0=Q and H_k=0 for k>0. This is not a claim that taking GL(V)-coinvariants preserves acyclicity.
hypotheses: F is infinite
V has finite dimension n>0
proofSteps: A chain has finite support. Collect the spans of all subtuples of length at most n-1 appearing in its support; each span is proper by genericity and dimension.
Use finite-subspace-avoidance to choose a vector v outside all these spans. Prepending v preserves genericity for the finite collection of tuples and faces needed in the computation.
The deletion identity gives boundary(cone_v z)=z-cone_v(boundary z). For a cycle the second term vanishes. In augmented degree zero use its zero augmentation.
The augmentation is surjective because n>0 provides a nonzero vector. This identifies the remaining H_0 with Q.
acceptance: The chosen cone depends on the finite chain; no global GL(V)-equivariant contracting homotopy is asserted.
The induced group-homology comparison still requires a projective-resolution comparison argument, recorded in G-TRILOG-MAP.

sources.match: The short source proof is expanded with its finite-support and augmentation conditions.

nodes.title: Weight three from the actual first-cycle comparison
nodes.statement: Given a Q-linear c3:K5(F)_Q->H^1(Gamma(F,3)), and a proof that its first-cycle evaluation equals a3 times the normalized Borel regulator for a3 in Q nonzero, the weight-three existential Zagier determinant follows. This conditional theorem does not construct c3; that proof subtree is G-TRILOG-MAP and G-TRILOG-REGULATOR.
hypotheses: F is a number field
c3 lands in actual first cohomology of the fixed complex
The specified nonzero rational regulator comparison holds
proofSteps: Use first-cohomology to regard c3 as a map into Z3(F).
Apply borel-matrix-input at n=3, then existential-transfer to c3 and the scalar a3.
Keep the raw-symbol tensor condition in G91 Theorem 1 separate: it is not used as a replacement for the assumed first-cycle condition.
acceptance: No arbitrary-weight motivic isomorphism is assumed.
The full unconditional stage is not realised merely by supplying this conditional theorem.

sources.match: These are the source's two necessary inputs. Their intermediate proofs are explicitly not closed in this packet.
The announcement's raw tensor condition is weaker data than the first-cycle target used here.

nodes.title: Lift uniquely through the kernel in a short exact sequence
nodes.statement: Given Q-linear j:B->L and p:L->E with j injective and image(j)=ker(p), construct the canonical Q-linear equivalence B->ker(p), b mapped to j(b). Its inverse is the unique preimage under j and is natural in commuting maps of such data. Surjectivity of p is not needed for this kernel equivalence.
hypotheses: j is injective
image(j)=ker(p)
proofSteps: Restrict j to ker(p) using p(j(b))=0.
The image equality gives surjectivity onto the kernel, and injectivity is inherited from j.
The inverse preserves addition and rational scalar multiplication because j is linear and injective; naturality follows from the same uniqueness argument.
acceptance: No arbitrary choice of a splitting of L->E is needed.
The construction is meaningful only after the exact-kernel theorem has been proved.

api.name: Zagier.exactKernelEquiv
api.statement: The canonical equivalence B->ker(p).

api.name: Zagier.exactKernelLift
api.statement: The unique b with j(b)=l for l in ker(p).

api.name: Zagier.exactKernelLift_spec
api.statement: Applying j to the lift recovers l, and this property determines the lift.

api.name: Zagier.exactKernelLift_natural
api.statement: Compatible maps of kernel data commute with the lift.

sources.match: An elementary kernel-lifting lemma motivated by the source's weight-four extension; the extension itself is not assumed proved by this lemma.

nodes.title: Remove the extra weight-two-wedge-weight-two component
nodes.statement: In exact-kernel-lift, suppose dB:B->T and dL:L->T are Q-linear and dL composed with j=dB. Set delta(l)=(dL(l),p(l)) in T direct-sum E. Then j induces a natural Q-linear equivalence ker(dB)->ker(delta). In the intended application B=B4(F), L is the auxiliary weight-four coalgebra piece and E=exterior-square B2(F).
hypotheses: All hypotheses of exact-kernel-lift
dL composed with j=dB
proofSteps: If dB(b)=0, both components of delta(j(b)) vanish.
If delta(l)=0 then p(l)=0, so exactKernelLift gives unique b with j(b)=l. Its dB value is dL(l)=0.
The two constructions are inverse by injectivity of j and its kernel-image property, and linearity and naturality restrict from exactKernelEquiv.
acceptance: A class in the auxiliary L4 is not sent to B4 until its (2,2)-cobracket vanishes.
This is a cycle-level equivalence; do not assert a full complex quasi-isomorphism without checking the remaining degrees.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.14 and Theorem 6.1, the weight-four extension and cobracket components
sources.match: Isolates the elementary cycle transport used after the source's difficult extension and compatibility theorems. Those are G-WEIGHT4-COALGEBRA.

nodes.title: Weight four after the flag and regulator constructions
nodes.statement: For a number field F, a Q-linear c4:K7(F)_Q->H^1(Gamma(F,4)) whose cycle evaluation is a4 times the normalized Borel regulator, for a4 in Q nonzero, implies the weight-four existential determinant identity with a nonzero rational prefactor. This does not prove that c4 is an isomorphism or establish rationality for every cycle tuple.
hypotheses: The weight-four complex and its first-cycle evaluation have been supplied
The actual c4 and its nonzero rational regulator comparison are given
proofSteps: Transport H^1 to first cycles using first-cohomology.
Use borel-matrix-input at n=4 and apply existential-transfer with a4.
When c4 is built through the auxiliary coalgebra, use compatible-cycle-lift only after the exactness and cobracket compatibility are proved.
For d=0 retain the rational prefactor; do not apply absorb-coefficient without its nonempty hypothesis.
acceptance: G-WEIGHT4-COALGEBRA, G-WEIGHT4-FLAGS and G-WEIGHT4-REGULATOR remain requirements for the unconditional theorem.
The rank-filtration comparison conjecture in GR is not promoted to an isomorphism theorem.

sources.match: The source supplies a map and a regulator relation, whereas the stronger isomorphism is separately conjectural. This node is expressly conditional on constructing that map.

nodes.title: The existential determinant assertion
nodes.statement: For a number field F and n>=2 with the supplied cycle carrier and evaluation, define ZagierExistence(F,n) to mean there is a d(F,n)-tuple x in Z_n(F) and q in Q nonzero such that zeta_F(n)=P(F,n,abs(disc F))*q*det M(lambda_n,x). This predicate contains an actual equality and actual cycles; it does not define either side by the other.
hypotheses: The zeta value, discriminant, cycle carrier and evaluation are already constructed
proofSteps: Quantify over the finite tuple of the existing cycle carrier and the nonzero rational coefficient.
Use the existing evaluation matrix and ordinary real equality after the supplier's real-value comparison for zeta(n).
acceptance: An all-weight theorem is not introduced by naming this predicate.
No expected dimension is built into the definition of B_n.

api.name: Zagier.Existence
api.statement: The explicit existential determinant predicate.

api.name: Zagier.Existence.witness
api.statement: A proof provides a tuple of cycles and its nonzero rational factor.

api.name: Zagier.Existence_iff
api.statement: Unfold exactly the tuple, coefficient and equality, without auxiliary assumptions.

sources.match: This is one precise assertion extracted from the formulation, kept separate from stronger comparison statements.

nodes.title: The universal rationality assertion
nodes.statement: For F,n as above with zeta_F(n)!=0, define ZagierAllTuples(F,n) to mean that for every d(F,n)-tuple x in Z_n(F), the real number P(F,n,abs(disc F))*det M(lambda_n,x)/zeta_F(n) is the image of some rational number. That rational may be zero.
hypotheses: The positive-integer zeta value is nonzero
proofSteps: Use membership in the image of Q->R, or equivalently an existential rational witness, for each tuple.
Do not add nonzero determinant as a hidden admissibility requirement.
acceptance: Every linearly dependent tuple is included and yields zero.
This predicate does not imply existence of a nonzero determinant without a separate spanning input.

api.name: Zagier.AllTuples
api.statement: The universally quantified rationality predicate.

api.name: Zagier.AllTuples.apply
api.statement: Apply the predicate to any tuple of actual cycles.

api.name: Zagier.AllTuples_zeroDet
api.statement: A zero determinant has rational ratio zero, since the denominator is nonzero.

sources.match: The stronger all-tuples clause is represented as its own assertion and proof obligation.

nodes.title: A stronger first-cycle comparison assertion
nodes.statement: For a number field F and n>=2, define FirstCycleComparison(F,n) as the existence of a Q-linear equivalence c:K_(2n-1)(F)_Q->Z_n(F), together with a nonzero rational a satisfying lambda_n composed with c=a*r_n in the fixed real coordinates. This is a number-field first-degree assertion, not the arbitrary-field all-degree motivic comparison conjecture.
hypotheses: The actual K-group, cycle carrier and both regulators have been constructed
proofSteps: Quantify over equivalences of the already constructed Q-vector spaces and a rational scalar witness.
Record the map-level equality as part of the proposition, never as an instance enabling unconditional theorem statements.
acceptance: An equivalence of bare abstract vector spaces without the regulator square does not satisfy the predicate.
Rank filtration and Adams weight are not identified in this definition.

api.name: Zagier.FirstCycleComparison
api.statement: The explicit comparison proposition.

api.name: Zagier.FirstCycleComparison.equiv
api.statement: A witness contains the actual equivalence, not just equality of dimensions.

api.name: Zagier.FirstCycleComparison.regulator_square
api.statement: The equality relates the two specified real-coordinate maps with a nonzero rational scalar.

sources.locator: Section 1 conjectural framework and Corollary 5.13, p. 46
sources.match: Distinguishes the conditional comparison framework from the determinant consequence and from an Adams-filtration claim.

nodes.title: The correct conditional implication
nodes.statement: For a number field F and n>=2, the Borel matrix input and FirstCycleComparison(F,n) imply both ZagierExistence(F,n) and ZagierAllTuples(F,n). More weakly, a forward map with the regulator square implies existence; to obtain all-tuples rationality it suffices additionally to know the required rational regulator-image containment.
hypotheses: The Borel matrix theorem is available in the fixed coordinates
The specified comparison or weaker forward-map hypotheses hold
proofSteps: Use existential-transfer for existence.
For a comparison equivalence, lift every cycle to K-theory and expand it in the Borel rational basis, proving the Q-span hypothesis of all-tuples-transfer.
For the weaker statement, replace surjectivity by that Q-span hypothesis directly. No converse is asserted.
acceptance: A conjectural first-cycle comparison appears as an explicit hypothesis, not an imported unconditional result.
A full all-degree motivic theorem is not necessary for this implication.

sources.match: The source's conjectural-to-special-value direction motivates this explicit linear-algebra implication; the extra all-tuples hypothesis is stated rather than smuggled in.

nodes.title: A forward map does not control all evaluated elements
nodes.statement: Fix a real alpha not in the image of Q. Let V=Q, W=Q direct-sum Q, r(t)=t, c(t)=(t,0), and lambda(x,y)=x+alpha*y. Then lambda composed with c=r and the one-column tuple c(1) gives determinant one, but lambda(0,1)=alpha is not rational. Thus the forward comparison and a nonzero determinant do not imply all-tuples rationality.
hypotheses: alpha is not rational
proofSteps: Check the three maps are Q-linear and lambda(c(t))=t.
Evaluate the tuples (1,0) and (0,1); their one-by-one determinants are 1 and alpha respectively.
Take z=P=1 to see the first gives an existential determinant identity while the second violates the all-tuples ratio condition.
acceptance: This is a counterexample to a proposed logical implication, not a counterexample to a literature theorem about actual polylogarithmic cycles.

sources.match: The countertest is constructed and proved here using the one-by-one determinant formula.

gaps.title: G-BASELINE — remaining foundation-source audit
gaps.detail: The listed baseline declarations were opened at their pins. A complete pinned-source audit of the further tensor-localization, free rational module, group-action, homological-complex and exact zeta-evaluation APIs has not been performed. Search both pinned trees, inspect every proposed match, and promote nonroutine reductions into nodes. The elementary mathematical proofs supplied here are not claims that these additional APIs already exist.

gaps.title: G-NORMALIZATION — Borel coordinate and erratum audit
gaps.detail: Borel 1977 Theorem 6.2 uses a compact-dual/rational-determinant-line normalization. Its displayed powers of pi must be transported to the chosen real single-valued-polylogarithm coordinate; matching ranks does not perform that transport. The 1980 erratum was located but its text was inaccessible. Read it, fix a single normalization ledger, and verify the functional-equation and Borel/Beilinson scalars with the supplier. No exact scalar is invented here.

gaps.title: G-DILOG — weight-two configuration and regulator comparison
gaps.detail: The read Zagier passages state and motivate the result but do not close a complete Suslin-map-to-Borel-map proof. Read the proof-level Bloch/Dupont–Sah or equivalent primary construction; split the cross-ratio cocycle, bar/configuration map, compatibility with the Suslin quotient, continuous-cohomology comparison, volume or Chern-class normalization, and arithmetic specialization into separate declarations. The geometric statement allowing algebraic parameters in an extension of F of degree at most four is not by itself the required F-rational Bloch-cycle theorem.

gaps.title: G-TRILOG-MAP — from the generic resolution to K5 cycles
gaps.detail: Continue GSEA section 3 after the inspected pp. 16–17. Specify f4,f5,f6 on generators, with its unnormalized Alt convention, and split each of delta*f5=f4*d, delta*f6=f5*d and f6*d=0. Prove their relation-model descent, volume-form independence and degeneracy identities. Construct the comparison from a projective bar resolution to the augmented generic complex; acyclicity does not imply coinvariant exactness. Construct the higher-rank/dual-Grassmannian comparison, stabilization and primitive K-theory map. Keep the source's rank filtration distinct from Adams weight. G91 Theorem 1's raw Delta-kernel condition is not a replacement for ker(delta3) in B2 tensor F-multiplicative.

gaps.title: G-TRILOG-REGULATOR — section 5's missing Chern-class subtree
gaps.detail: The statement and concluding proof of GSEA Theorem 5.11 were read: they require Theorems 5.8 and 5.10 and the Beilinson/Borel comparison. Decompose the actual regulator morphism from the polylogarithmic complex to the Deligne complex, its residue compatibility, the explicit universal third Chern cocycle, independence and normalization, and the sphere-period computation giving rationality. Follow Proposition 5.7, the local examples and Lemmas 5.3–5.4 to source-level lemmas. These intermediate proofs have not been fully inspected, so the main comparison is an explicit hypothesis in the current conditional endpoint.

gaps.title: G-WEIGHT4-COALGEBRA — relations and exact extension
gaps.detail: Build GR's auxiliary weight<=4 symbol spaces, the (3,1) symbols and relations, and split the cobracket descent/co-Jacobi theorem into its relation checks. Decompose Theorem 6.1's map L4/B4->exterior-square B2, antisymmetry, five-term descent, inverse and injectivity calculations, including Lemma 6.4 and Corollary 6.5. Prove the (3,1)-cobracket restriction agrees with delta4 on B4. The elementary exact-kernel and compatible-cycle lemmas in this packet then apply. The hard extension theorem is not established merely by citing those elementary lemmas.

gaps.title: G-WEIGHT4-FLAGS — decorated flags, Bigrassmannian and symbolic identities
gaps.detail: Decompose GR sections 2–7 and 10: motivic-correlator realization and its relations; the necessary cluster/flip identities; decorated-flag configurations and their differential; the map to the auxiliary weight-four Chevalley complex; the dual Bigrassmannian maps and every component of Theorem 7.6; rescaling invariance in Lemma 7.7; stabilization and the rank-three vanishing homotopy. Section 10's explicit symbolic chain identities need exact rational coefficient certificates and sign conventions. The source says the representation-stability alternative is not needed; do not import it as a prerequisite. The inspected theorem endpoints do not amount to a complete reading or decomposition of these proof sections.

gaps.title: G-WEIGHT4-REGULATOR — residues and fourth Chern normalization
gaps.detail: Decompose GR sections 8–9 and their cited regulator sources into the Deligne morphism, residue compatibility and extension from generic configurations, Lemma 9.3's collinear trilogarithm identity, Corollary 9.4's residue vanishing, and the universal fourth Chern class comparison in Theorem 9.1. Read the cited primary Beilinson comparison and track the Tate-coordinate scalar. Show that specialization to complex embeddings yields a nonzero rational multiple of the exact Borel map in G-NORMALIZATION. Do not replace this by the fact that the continuous-cohomology group is one-dimensional.

gaps.title: G-ALL-TUPLES — higher-weight reverse regulator-image control
gaps.detail: A map from K-theory into cycles with a compatible regulator proves existence, but does not by itself put the regulator of every cycle into the same rational K-theory span. To recover the all-tuples clauses, construct and verify the needed reverse motivic realization/image-containment theorem for the exact relation model, or an appropriate comparison equivalence, without assuming the separately stated general conjecture. The forward-map-countertest demonstrates the missing logical input; it does not assert an error in the source theorem.

gaps.title: G-GENERAL-STATEMENT — arbitrary fields and all cohomological degrees
gaps.detail: The packet specifies the number-field first-degree comparison. The roadmap also requires the stronger arbitrary-field comparison in the source's exact proven or conjectured degree range. Construct the Adams or gamma graded pieces and the polylogarithmic cohomology objects through their owners, formulate that separate conjecture with its degree restrictions and functoriality, and record any rank-filtration-to-Adams comparison as another theorem. This part has not yet been converted to declaration-sized nodes.

gaps.title: G-SOURCE-PROVENANCE — missing downloadable bytes
gaps.detail: All public references listed were accessed through browser text and/or PDF screenshots, but direct downloads into the execution environment failed. Archive the exact source versions and compute SHA-256 when bytes are available. The present packet records edition, URL and access date without inventing content hashes.

restructure.detail: Polylogarithms P.2–P.4 already contain some K-theory regulator comparisons, low-weight zeta consequences and general statement infrastructure, while this design job assigns those application proof chains to the new roadmap. The reserved Bloch-Wigner IDs are assigned to K3BlochGroups although some analytic construction is repeated in Polylogarithms P.1.
restructure.proposal: Keep the canonical integral/rational Bloch carriers, enhanced-torsion exact sequence and the reserved weight-two function/relations with K3BlochGroups; keep the reusable higher functions, relation quotients and complexes with Polylogarithms; keep Borel ranks, regulator lattices, zeta and Borel/Beilinson coordinate comparison with BorelRegulators. Let this roadmap own the proof-specific configuration/correlator comparisons and determinant applications. Remove application conclusions from supplier prerequisites after orchestrator reconciliation, never by editing those files in this job. A n=3 application theorem must not depend on a supplier's same n=3 zeta theorem.
